title: Anaphylaxis after peanuts, 16-year-old in restaurant

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: My friend is having an allergic reaction, she ate something with peanuts! We're at a restaurant!

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Uh, the Thai place on Klostergatan, Klostergatan 5 in Lund.

transcript.speaker: operator
transcript.text: How old is she and how is she now?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: She's 16. Her lips are swelling up really fast and she's scratching her neck.

transcript.speaker: operator
transcript.text: Is she having any trouble breathing?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: She says her throat feels tight. And her voice sounds weird, kind of hoarse. [background: is she okay?]

transcript.speaker: operator
transcript.text: Does she have an EpiPen, an adrenaline pen?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Yes, it's in her bag, but she said she wants to wait and see if it gets better.

transcript.speaker: operator
transcript.text: She needs to use it now. Take the pen, blue cap off, press the orange tip hard into the outside of her thigh, through the jeans is fine, and hold for three seconds.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Okay okay, I'm doing it... done. I held it.

transcript.speaker: operator
transcript.text: Good. I'm sending an ambulance with sirens. Let her sit if she's breathing badly, or lie down with legs up if she feels faint.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: She says she feels dizzy now.

transcript.speaker: operator
transcript.text: Then lay her down with her legs up. Does she have a second pen?
